title: Fix quota enforcement edge case causing 429 misclassification + inconsistent rate-limit headers
creator: Ethan Park
body:
Context
- Reported by Support during known-issues sprint triage.
- Primary tickets: SUP-1843 (unexpected 429 after upgrading SDK), SUP-1855 (rate limit headers inconsistent across endpoints).
- Symptoms: customers see 429s that look like quota exhaustion while dashboard/contracted limits show remaining capacity. Separately, RateLimit headers (and sometimes Retry-After) are inconsistent across endpoints and can differ between initial and fallback-routed responses.

Problem statement
- We have an edge case in quota enforcement when requests are routed through a fallback path (or when a request hits a per-route limiter after account quota evaluation).
- In some cases we:
  (a) classify the 429 as "quota_exceeded" even when the failure is a per-route rate limit (burst) or concurrency limiter, and
  (b) emit RateLimit-* headers computed from a different policy bucket than the one that actually rejected the request (e.g., headers reflect the pre-fallback route or the account-level quota bucket, while the 429 originates from a downstream limiter).
- Result: customers and Support cannot reliably interpret whether they should retry, reduce burst, or request quota changes. It also increases escalations because headers appear "wrong" vs Console limits.

Root cause (confirmed)
- Gateway composes the 429 response using a "best available" limiter context. Under fallback routing we may lose the original limiter decision metadata and we fall back to account-quota context.
- The header formatter and the error classifier were not using the same "source of truth". Header emission chose the first populated context; classification chose a different branch (quota-first).
- Some endpoints were on an older header formatter path (legacy RateLimit headers) while others used the new formatter, leading to cross-endpoint inconsistency.

Proposed fix
1) Unify limiter decision + header generation
- Introduce a single RateLimitDecision object that is produced at the point of rejection and is passed through to response composition.
- Ensure both classification (error code) and header emission consume the same decision object.

2) Correct classification for 429
- If rejection source == route limiter / concurrency limiter: classify as rate_limited and include Retry-After when available.
- If rejection source == account quota: classify as quota_exceeded.
- If multiple limiters are involved, prefer the rejecting limiter (the one that returned deny).

3) Standardize headers across endpoints
- Always emit a consistent set:
  - RateLimit-Limit
  - RateLimit-Remaining
  - RateLimit-Reset
  - Retry-After (only when meaningful; otherwise omit)
- Add an internal-only debug header for Support/SRE verification:
  - x-redwood-ratelimit-source: account_quota | route_limiter | concurrency_limiter
  (flagged behind internal/allowlist so it does not leak broadly)

4) Preserve behavior for clients
- Status code remains 429.
- Do not change response schema beyond the error classification string/code (align with existing error envelope).

Scope / non-goals
- Not changing actual quota/rate-limit policies or default thresholds.
- Not changing plan entitlements or billing.
- Not retrofitting all historical logs; we will add forward-looking structured logs.

Implementation notes
- Touch points:
  - gateway/rate_limit middleware
  - fallback routing handler (ensure decision metadata preserved)
  - error classifier mapping
  - header formatter (remove legacy path; keep compatibility shim)
- Logging:
  - Emit structured field ratelimit.source and ratelimit.bucket_id to enable correlation with dashboards.

Acceptance criteria
- For fallback-routed requests that fail with 429:
  - error classification matches the rejecting limiter.
  - RateLimit-* headers reflect the same limiter bucket.
- Headers are consistent across endpoints (chat/generate/embeddings/rerank).
- Support can validate rejection source without asking Engineering (via allowlisted debug header + logs).
- Regression coverage added for:
  - fallback path
  - mixed limiter evaluation
  - legacy endpoint routes

References / links
- Support tickets: SUP-1843, SUP-1855
- Related work: ENG-4821 (support signal for fallback metrics), ENG-4823 (dashboard links)
- Docs/KB: workaround-429-quota-mismatch-and-rate-limit-headers (Support article)
- Code change: PR redwood#19322 (fix rate-limit header consistency + tests)

Rollout plan
- Phase 0 (staging): Validate with synthetic load + forced fallback routing; confirm header consistency and classification.
- Phase 1 (canary): 5% traffic in us-east for Hosted; monitor 429 rate, Retry-After presence, and support-reported anomalies.
- Phase 2: Roll to all Hosted regions.
- Phase 3: Roll to Dedicated control-plane gateways (coordinate with SRE for change window); verify no customer-specific header expectations break.
- Backout: revert gateway deploy; old behavior returns. No data migrations.

Monitoring
- Dashboards/alerts:
  - 429 rate by endpoint + region
  - ratelimit.source distribution (expect shift: fewer "quota_exceeded" classifications for burst-limited cases)
  - Support escalations tagged "quota/rate limit confusion" (qualitative)

Support enablement
- Post in #support once canary passes with:
  - what changed (classification + headers)
  - how to interpret new behavior
  - when to escalate (suspected genuine quota mismatch after fix)
- Update known-issues article to note "fixed as of control-plane-2026.02" and keep workaround guidance for older stacks.
test_plan:
Automated
- Unit tests:
  - rate_limit_classifier_prefers_rejecting_limiter
  - header_formatter_uses_decision_bucket
  - legacy_routes_use_standard_formatter
- Integration tests (gateway):
  - forced_fallback_route_limiter_429_emits_route_bucket_headers
  - account_quota_429_emits_quota_bucket_headers
  - concurrency_limiter_429_sets_retry_after_when_available

Manual
- Using internal load tool:
  - Trigger route limiter on /v1/chat.completions and verify headers + error code.
  - Trigger fallback routing then trigger limiter; verify headers reflect fallback route bucket.
  - Compare behavior across endpoints (chat/generate/embeddings/rerank) for consistency.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge PR redwood#19322 behind feature flag: ratelimit.decision_v2 (default on in staging).
2) Staging soak (30–60 min) with synthetic traffic + forced fallback.
3) Production canary (us-east, 5%): 1–2 hours, watch 429/error classification mix and customer reports.
4) Global Hosted rollout.
5) Dedicated/Private: include in next control-plane gateway update window; notify CSMs for accounts with prior tickets.
6) Update KB + Support macros once rollout complete.
comments: 2026-02-06 (Ethan Park): Created after Support escalation review. This is blocking clean guidance for SUP-1843/SUP-1855; customers are interpreting 429s as hard quota exhaustion.

2026-02-07 (Mina Haddad): I can reproduce via forced fallback in staging; headers reflect pre-fallback route bucket while rejection occurs post-fallback. Agree on passing a single decision object through response composition.

2026-02-08 (Sean Gallagher): Please ensure classification aligns with paging thresholds/incident comms. If we mislabel as quota_exceeded, Support tends to treat it as account issue vs incident. Add structured logging so we can verify in aggregate.
2026-02-10 (Priya Shah): Support request: add a reliable signal we can quote in tickets. Internal-only x-redwood-ratelimit-source would be ideal (allowlist).
2026-02-12 (Mina Haddad): PR up (redwood#19322). Added integration tests for fallback + limiter. Also removed legacy header path for embeddings endpoint that was causing mismatch.
2026-02-14 (Ethan Park): Canary plan approved. Please post in #support after us-east canary passes so we can update macros and close loop on SUP-1843/1855.

2026-02-18 (Mina Haddad): Rolled out globally for Hosted. Metrics look stable; classification mix shifted as expected. Follow-up: ensure Dedicated gateway release notes include header standardization to avoid surprises.
